chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn al-Husayn al-Warraq) from Safwan from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

"Send forward the children who are with you to Al-Juhfa or to the valley of Mar, then do with them what is done with the Muhrim (one in Ihram): they are circumambulated, they run (Sa'i), and stones are thrown on their behalf. And whoever among them does not have a sacrificial animal, his guardian should fast on his behalf."

The child is kept away from everything that the Muhrim must avoid, and all that the Muhrim must do is done for him. And if he does something for which a penalty (Kaffarah) is required, it is upon his guardian to compensate for it. Narrated.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: one in the state of Ihram (sacred consecration for Hajj)
key_terms.يُرْمَى عَنْهُمْ: stones are thrown on their behalf (performing Rami)

ai.seo_question: What are the Hajj rituals and penalties for children accompanying their parents?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the legal mechanism of vicarious performance (*niyabah*) in Hajj, where guardians act on behalf of children who lack full legal capacity (*ahliyyah*). It establishes that children are subject to the same prohibitions and rituals as adult pilgrims, with the guardian bearing the financial and ritual responsibility for any penalties (*kaffarah*) incurred due to the child's actions or omissions.
